items.title: Google Study: Gated Self-Improving Harnesses Take a Coding Agent from 5% to 40% Success
items.summary: The paper 'Harnesses That Improve Themselves' argues that the runtime around a model - context and state, agent control, action interfaces, and verification and recovery - matters as much as the weights. An optimizer edits one of four code modules at a time on a 142-line seed harness; every edit must survive a held-out validation set and a token cap. With a frozen Gemini 3.8 Flash on 40 unseen SWE-bench Lite tasks, the gated harness improved from 5.0% to 40.0% at roughly 46.7k tokens per task. Unrestricted full rewrites scored slightly higher at 42.5% but consumed about 451.6k tokens per task, nearly ten times more, while encoding the lessons as prompt rules alone dropped accuracy to 2.5%. A companion Google paper, GUARD, reports 80.80% on 43 hosted SDK tasks (+8.89 points, 54.5% fewer tokens) by letting the agent edit its own prompts, skills, tool rules and memory while the base model stays frozen.
items.impact: This reframes agent reliability as an engineering problem that can be improved without retraining: gate every harness change on held-out tasks AND cost, and enforce hard constraints in code rather than in prompts. The design matters for any vertical-domain agent pipeline, because a harness tuned for one model often regresses on the next. The caution is equally useful - a naive 'keep whatever scores better' gate mostly selects noise, so the verifier must sit outside the agent's write access.

items.title: OpenAI Models Rewrite RTL: Up to 14% PPA Gain on AMD's Flagship GPU IP
items.summary: In 'Advancing chip design with OpenAI models', OpenAI reports that its models rewrote SystemVerilog RTL for a heavily optimized AMD flagship GPU IP block and achieved up to 14% improvement in power, performance and area, compressing about a year of optimization work into under five months. AMD has folded some changes into a recent tape-out and stored others in production design files for future versions; its next-generation flagship CPU showed single-digit PPA gains in key blocks. On OpenAI's own Jalapeño inference chip, model-proposed edits cut standard-cell area by about 13% in the vector unit and 10% in the matrix unit, with one multiplier redesign shrinking area ~15% while dropping from two clock cycles to one. On open-source PicoRV32 and Ibex RISC-V cores, GPT-6.2 Astra scored highest under a roughly 112k-token budget. OpenAI is now training a GPT-Synopsys model to work inside professional EDA flows.
items.impact: This is AI coding pushed past software into physical design: the model proposes circuit changes, EDA tools check functional equivalence and PPA, and engineers decide what ships. The 14% figure is a block-level maximum against a high baseline, not a whole-GPU gain, and silicon measurements are still outstanding - but AMD putting changes into tape-out is a genuine adoption signal. Expect the same generator / verifier / gate pattern to spread to other safety-critical engineering work.

items.title: Meta Says AI Agents Now Handle Over 60% of Ad-Model Technique Propagation
items.summary: Meta detailed its Ranking Engineer Agent (REA), an autonomous system that generates hypotheses, designs experiments and proves new machine-learning techniques on ads ranking models, then propagates validated techniques across a fleet of models with different architectures and data. Meta estimates agents have handled over 60% of all technique propagation since they began driving execution in March 2026. Early results include three times more technique-model adaptations per engineer, a median fourfold reduction in training compute across selected technique-model combinations, and an estimated $45M+ in compute savings by year end. All figures are Meta's own internal estimates.
items.impact: This is one of the clearest ROI accounts for a production coding agent so far: savings are expressed in GPU time and engineer throughput rather than benchmark points. It also sketches a workable division of labour, with agents running experiments and porting proven techniques while humans set direction and judge outcomes. For teams adopting agents, the metric worth tracking is cost per completed migration, not lines of code generated.

items.title: APEC Shenzhen Puts Seven Humanoids into Real Press-Center Service
items.summary: During the 2026 APEC Leaders' Week in Shenzhen, local startup Zhipingfang Robotics placed seven humanoids in the press center, serving more than 5,000 Chinese and foreign journalists coffee, ice cream and soft drinks. The robots used standard commercial coffee, ice-cream and juice machines rather than purpose-built dispensers, and were driven by an in-house model instead of large scripted flows; the company says unfamiliar tables, equipment layouts and lighting at the venue barely affected performance. Roughly 2,000 volunteers ran wave-based safety and stress tests, including challenges issued by the press center, before the robots were certified for on-site work. The company says commercial discussions are under way with more than a third of APEC economies, including Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, South Korea and Australia.
items.impact: Unlike stage demos, this is unscripted service in a high-traffic, changing environment with an explicit safety-certification process - a practical test of whether embodied models generalize beyond the venues they were trained in. It also shows the likely commercial path: familiar service tasks performed with human tools first, with international buyers watching closely. The figures are company-reported, and independent data on uptime and cost per serving is still missing.

items.title: Spanish Plant Pilot: Unitree Robot Learns a New Task from 12 Demos in 11 Minutes
items.summary: French auto-parts supplier Novares, robotics integrator Innov8 and startup Bleu Robotics published pilot results from a plant in Sesena, Spain, using a Unitree platform for part recognition, pick-and-place and boxing. The companies report 100% part recognition, 99.5% pick-and-place success, 95% success placing boxes, and 200 autonomous cycles across 60 minutes. Most notably, the robot learned its first task from just 12 human demonstrations in 11 minutes. The figures are company-reported pilot results, not independently verified long-run production data.
items.impact: The headline number is skill-acquisition cost: 12 demos and 11 minutes makes short-run, mixed-SKU factory work far more plausible than months of bespoke programming. But 200 cycles is a tiny sample beside the tens of thousands a production line demands, so the next gates are task transfer, reliability drift and cost per unit. It fits a broader pattern this week - automation buyers are starting to ask for cycle time, uptime and unit economics instead of humanoid spectacle.
